**Integrative Cardiopulmonary & Renal Physiology** ★★ — Pressure/flow gradients, V/Q & O₂ kinetics, renal arteriolar/tubular control, and shock profiles govern every bedside threshold.

- **Flow (Shock / Haemorrhage):** Volume/pump/tone loss → ↓DO₂ → anaerobic lactate ==>2 mmol/L== → classify PCWP × CO × SVR × SvO₂ → restore delivery without exhausting reserve (never push fluids on flat Frank-Starling limb).

## Core physiological thresholds ★★

| System | Parameter | Value / Formula | Clinical boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Cardiac AP** ★ | Resting Vm / QTc | Ventricular ==-90 mV== · SA ==-60 mV== · QTc >450 M / >470 F | Phase 2 ICa,L prevents tetanus; SA Phase 0 = ICa,L only; check QTc/K⁺/Mg²⁺ first |
| **Pump / PV** ★ | EF / CO / SVR | EF ==55-70 %== (<40 % HFrEF) · CO 5 L/min · SVR ==800-1,200== | CPP = DBP - LVEDP; S4 ==never== heard in AF |
| **Ventilation** ★★ | ARDS targets | VT ==6 mL/kg predicted BW== (==never actual==) · Pplat ==≤30 cmH₂O== | Driving P <15 cmH₂O; high Ppeak + normal Pplat (>5 diff) = airway resistance |
| **Gas exchange** ★★ | A-a / SpO₂ / P50 | Normal A-a <10-15 · P50 27 mmHg · COPD SpO₂ ==88-92 %== | True R→L shunt ==does not== normalise on 100% O₂; PaO₂ <60 triggers carotid body |
| **Renal** ★★ | GFR / autoreg | GFR ==120-125 mL/min== · MAP ==80-180 mmHg== · FF ~20 % | NSAIDs constrict afferent (↓GFR); ACEi/ARBs dilate efferent (↓GFR, ↓FF) |
| **Water / Na⁺** ★★ | Chronic hypoNa⁺ cap | Max ==≤8 mEq/L per 24 h== (4-6 high-risk) | Avoid osmotic demyelination syndrome (chronic hyperNa⁺ cap ≤10/24 h) |

## Shock phenotypes (vs) ★★

| Shock class | PCWP / CVP | CO | SVR | SvO₂ | Signature trap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Hypovolaemic** | ↓ | ↓ | ↑ | ↓ | Early Hb may look normal — ==never== exclude bleeding on 1 early Hb |
| **Cardiogenic** | ↑ | ↓ | ↑ | ↓ | Flat Starling limb → fluids worsen pulmonary oedema |
| **Obstructive** | ↑ | ↓ | ↑ | ↓ | Tension PTX, tamponade, massive PE |
| **Distributive** | ↓ / N | ↑ (early) | ↓ | ↑ / N | Neurogenic (>T6) = hypotension + **bradycardia**; anaphylaxis = **IM epinephrine ==0.3-0.5 mg==** first |

## High-yield discriminators

- **O₂ curve & dys-Hb ★★:** Right shift (↑unloading) = ↑CO₂, acidosis (Bohr), ↑2,3-BPG, exercise, ↑temp. **CO poisoning** (240× affinity, left shift) → falsely normal SpO₂ → co-oximetry + 100% O₂. **MetHb** → fixed ~85% SpO₂, chocolate blood → methylene blue 1-2 mg/kg (==avoid in severe G6PD deficiency==).
- **Nephron & diuretics ★★:** PCT reabsorbs 65-70% Na⁺ + 100% glucose (threshold ~180-200 mg/dL); **TAL (NKCC2)** diluting segment → **loops lose Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺**; **DCT (NCC)** → **thiazides retain Ca²⁺**; collecting duct ENaC (aldosterone) & AQP2 (ADH/V2).
- **Obstructive vs restrictive:** Obstructive = FEV1/FVC <0.70, ↑TLC/RV; restrictive = FEV1/FVC normal/high (>0.80), ↓TLC (<80%).

## ⚠ Never

- ==Never== give QT-prolonging antiarrhythmics without checking baseline QTc and correcting K⁺ and Mg²⁺ first.
- ==Do not== continue fluid loading once on the flat Frank-Starling limb.
- ==Never== use prolonged aggressive hyperventilation routinely in TBI ==except briefly as a rescue bridge during impending herniation==.
- ==Never== size ARDS tidal volume by actual weight in obesity (use ==6 mL/kg predicted body weight==).
- ==Never== combine NSAID + ACEi/ARB + diuretic ("triple whammy") casually in volume-depleted patients.
- ==Never== correct chronic hyponatraemia (>48 h) ==faster than 8 mEq/L in 24 h== (ODS).
- ==Never== rely on a single early normal haemoglobin to rule out acute haemorrhage, and ==never== delay IM epinephrine (0.3-0.5 mg) in anaphylaxis.

## Cards

- Why does cardiac Phase 2 prevent tetanic contraction, and what drives SA node Phase 0? → Prolonged Phase 2 L-type Ca²⁺ plateau creates a long effective refractory period; SA node Phase 0 relies exclusively on L-type Ca²⁺ channels (no fast Na⁺ channels)
- How do high Ppeak with normal Pplat vs high Ppeak with high Pplat differ? → High Ppeak + normal Pplat (gradient >5 cmH₂O) = elevated airway resistance; high Ppeak + high Pplat = reduced compliance (ARDS, oedema, pneumothorax)
- ARDS lung-protective tidal volume and pressure limits → 6 mL/kg predicted body weight (never actual weight), Pplat ≤30 cmH₂O, driving pressure <15 cmH₂O
- Why does a true right-to-left shunt fail to correct on 100% FiO₂? → Shunted mixed venous blood bypasses ventilated alveoli and never contacts alveolar gas (unlike V/Q mismatch)
- Effects of NSAIDs vs ACE inhibitors/ARBs on RPF, GFR, and filtration fraction → NSAIDs constrict afferent arteriole (↓RPF, ↓GFR, FF unchanged); ACEi/ARBs dilate efferent arteriole (↑RPF, ↓GFR, ↓FF); combining both + diuretic = triple whammy AKI
- Opposite calcium effects of loop vs thiazide diuretics → Loop diuretics block NKCC2 and abolish lumen-positive potential (lose Ca²⁺); thiazides block NCC and boost basolateral Na⁺/Ca²⁺ exchange (retain Ca²⁺)
- Maximum 24-hour correction limit for chronic hyponatraemia and its risk → Never faster than 8 mEq/L in 24 h (4-6 mEq/L in high-risk patients) to prevent osmotic demyelination syndrome
- Distinguishing bedside profile of neurogenic shock (above T6) vs hypovolaemic shock → Neurogenic: hypotension + warm extremities (↓SVR) + paradoxical bradycardia; hypovolaemic: ↓PCWP, ↓CO, ↑SVR, compensatory tachycardia, ↓SvO₂
